mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above 4% in a given month coincides with a decline in 20-day S&P 500 forward returns due to higher discounting of future cash flows.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4.0% in the current month
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window, 20-day forward returns remain non-negative despite persistent FEDFUNDS > 4.0%, or the inflation-adjusted real rate does not fall below 2%.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly rise in UNRATE above 7.5% coincides with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return as higher labor market rigidity reduces corporate investment demand.
failure_condition: In 20 consecutive months with UNRATE > 7.5%, the 20-day forward return is non-negative on more than 70% of occasions.

mechanism_narrative: When monthly GDPC1 (real private consumption) exceeds INDPRO by more than 5% for two consecutive months, it signals excess demand, leading to positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 - INDPRO > 5% for two consecutive months
regime_hint: Economic expansion with strong consumption pull
failure_condition: The two-month excess-demand condition recurs but is not followed by a positive 20-day forward return in >50% of cases over a 12-month window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in INDPRO of at least 8% for three consecutive months indicates softening supply constraints, which precedes a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls >8% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: Three-month INDPRO decline is followed by no statistically significant positive 60-day forward return (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS remains below 1% for four consecutive months in a non-recessionary regime, it predicts a positive 5-day S&P 500 forward return as investors anticipate future rate cuts.
failure_condition: Over 12 such months, the 5-day forward return never exceeds the 1-month lagged CPIAUCSL growth by more than 0.5 percentage points.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in PAYEMS below 120,000 in a month accompanied by a simultaneous rise in UNRATE above 6%, signals labor market weakness that precedes negative 20-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: The combined signal recurs but is not followed by a negative 20-day return in >80% of instances over 24 months.

mechanism_narrative: When monthly HOUST (household spending in thousands of units) rises faster than CPIAUCSL by more than 2% in the same month, it indicates demand acceleration and a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: HOUST growth rate > CPIAUCSL growth rate by >2% in a month
failure_condition: The HOUST-CPIAUCSL divergence triggers but is not followed by a positive 60-day forward return in >70% of cases over 18 months.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly RSAFS (retail sales) decline of 10% or more persists for two consecutive months in a non-crisis environment, predicting a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to reduced consumer confidence and spending.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS falls >10% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: The two-month RSAFS decline recurs but is not associated with a negative 20-day forward return in >60% of such events over 36 months.
